Pony.ai and Uber prepare Gen-7 robotaxi testing in London

The UK expansion is at the road-testing preparation stage, with fleet arrangements and passenger-service timing still undisclosed.

EVMagz ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

Preparing a new city trial

Pony.ai announced on October 8 that it was working with Uber to bring Gen-7 robotaxis to London, with testing expected in the coming weeks. It said it would work with local officials and partners as plans progress. This is preparation for trials, not confirmation of an open passenger service.

Building on a European partnership

The London plan follows the partners’ service in Zagreb, Croatia, where Pony.ai supplies autonomous-driving technology and Uber connects rides to its network. Ownership and operating arrangements for the London fleet have not been disclosed. The earlier city’s structure should not automatically be assumed to apply unchanged.

Details still to come

The announcement does not set a commercial-service date, fleet size, service area or London test safety-operator arrangements. Real-road results and operational details are still needed before drawing conclusions about when driverless service could begin or how extensively it could operate.
